name: swap_nonoverlapping_simple_untyped
declaration: const unsafe fn swap_nonoverlapping_simple_untyped < T > (x : * mut T , y : * mut T , count : usize)
documentation:
Same behavior and safety conditions as [`swap_nonoverlapping`]

 LLVM can vectorize this (at least it can for the power-of-two-sized types
 `swap_nonoverlapping` tries to use) so no need to manually SIMD it.
rules: Both `x` and `y` must be valid for both reads and writes of `count * size_of::<T>()` bytes.
Both `x` and `y` must be properly aligned for `T`, even when `count * size_of::<T>()` is zero.
The memory region beginning at `x` of size `count * size_of::<T>()` bytes must not overlap the memory region beginning at `y` of the same size.
The data in the regions may be uninitialized or otherwise violate the requirements of `T`.
The initialization state of the swapped data is preserved exactly.
